title: Understand Percent
objective: I can explain a percent as a rate per 100, model it on a decimal grid or tape diagram, and interpret percents greater than 100%.
model: 10 × 10 decimal grid (1 square = 1%), percent bar / tape diagram, and a ratio table scaled so the whole is 100; percents above 100% as more than one whole

widgets.component: interactive 10 × 10 grid: slider, drag-to-paint, +1 / +10 / preset buttons, tenths-line toggle; tiles show square counts only
widgets.root: A genuinely manipulable decimal grid. The tiles print 'Shaded / Not shaded / Whole grid' as square counts and never the percent, so the percent is the student's to say. Pointer events paint by element-from-point, so it works for touch and mouse.

widgets.where: Practice Tab 1 tasks 1-8 (mc, single, dual with 'what does it mean' check, triple, mc with 40% / 100% / 150% figure)
widgets.component: 8 guided cards driving the grid (percent means per 100, 9 of 100, 53/100, 0.71, 23 as fraction / decimal / percent, shaded and not shaded, columns of ten, less / equal / more than one whole)
widgets.root: On objective: percent as per-100, fraction and decimal hundredths, the complement, and the first look at 150%. Tasks 2-4 are near-restatements of the grid and task 1 is repeated as quiz q1; the 40 / 100 / 150 SVG in task 8 is proportional.

widgets.where: Practice Tab 2 (12 scale-to-100 problems + random generator)
widgets.component: ratio-machine cards: multiply the whole by what to make 100, scale the part, then choose the sentence that says what the percent means (from problem 2)
widgets.root: The lesson's worked example (4 of 10 -> 40 of 100) in a step-by-step card; wholes 4, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50 only, so every factor is whole. The meaning-check MC removes the copy-the-number step. Partitioned percent-bar SVG verified proportional.

widgets.where: Practice Tab 3 (8: 4 bar problems, 3 bridge-table problems, 1 multi-row camp table)
widgets.component: find 1 block on a percent bar, or divide to simplify then scale to 100, or scale a whole table by 4
widgets.root: Percent bar and ratio table are the lesson's representations; arithmetic verified (20 pts / 4 blocks = 25% each, 9 of 12 = 3 of 4 = 75%, 14 / 7 / 4 of 25 = 56 / 28 / 16%). Static bar, typed answers.

widgets.where: Practice Tab 4 (8 word problems / error detective, static bar SVGs)
widgets.component: complement (11 of 20 used a coupon), 50 students with a turtle remainder, $750 of a $500 goal = 150%, Kira 60% versus Dev 80%, 12/25 ≠ 12%, +90 additive scaling, shaded versus not shaded, 14 oz versus 8 oz = 175%
widgets.root: Percents above 100% and the additive-scaling misconception are exactly the lesson's two traps. All eight SVG bars checked against their numbers (e.g. 297 + 243 of 540). 'Percentage points' (item 4) is a term the lesson's vocabulary does not define.

widgets.component: mastery check: meaning, 3 of 10, 65 of 100, more than one whole, 1.5 times = 150%, 9 of 25, 33 of 50, 9 of 12, complement, justify 150%
widgets.root: On objective; keys correct; feedback for each wrong choice.

widgets.where: Practice Bonus Round (assets/u4-studio-bonus.js, gen pctMeaning, 4 rounds)
widgets.component: 'Match the Trios': tap three of nine tiles that go together, e.g. '40%', '40 out of 100', '0.4'
widgets.root: Each trio is the same fact in three spellings, so it asks for recall of 'percent means per 100' and for moving a decimal, not for reasoning about a model; the wrong guesses just clear the selection.
widgets.replacement: Rebuild as 'name the grid': show a 10 × 10 grid (or two grids plus part of a third for rounds 3-4) shaded to p, and three tiles to choose among: the correct percent, the complement 100 − p, and p ÷ 10. A miss names which confusion it was (shaded versus not shaded; tenths versus hundredths). Keep the star scoring and no timer.

widgets.where: Challenge Section 1 items s1_e1-e3, s1_6, s1_1, s1_2, s1_7, s1_8 (grid visuals)
widgets.component: count squares, three forms of 53 / 100, shaded and not shaded, 9/25 and 7/20 scaled to 100, 235% on three grids, half a square = 0.5% = 1/200, 1.8 times as tall, which statement about 0.5% is true
widgets.root: Percents above 100% and below 1% on a grid are the lesson's own extensions; static gridVisual draws the extra grids and the zoomed square correctly. (s1_8 uses 1/200, which the core page's reference card also states.)

widgets.where: Challenge Section 1 items s1_3, s1_4, s1_5 and quiz q1, q2 (math/unit-4/percent-practice-studio-challenging/)
widgets.component: 3/8 as a decimal and percent ('find 1/8 first'), 0.065 and 2.4 as percents, order 1/2, 55%, 0.6, 5/8, greatest of 0.7 / 65% / 3/4 / 7/10, 0.4% as a decimal
widgets.root: Converting between fractions, decimals and percents and ordering mixed forms is lesson 4-2's objective (and the 4-2 core page teaches the slider that does it). Lesson 4-1 only establishes 1% = 0.01 = 1/100 on the grid.
widgets.replacement: Delete these five items. Replace with grid-only 4-1 extensions: (a) a paint-the-grid task, 'shade 135%': the student paints up to two grids to a target and the checker reads the painted count; (b) 'half a square': shade half of one cell and give the percent and 'how many of these squares make a whole grid'; (c) 'order by shaded amount' using three grids (0.7 of a grid, 65 squares, 7 columns), no symbols; (d) quiz replacements: percent as a rate per 100 for 3 of 4 (75%) and for 9/8 on 2 grids (112.5%).

widgets.where: Challenge Section 2 (13: simplify, then scale to 100)
widgets.root: The lesson's method (equivalent ratios to 100) with a simplification bridge and decimal factors (12.5, 2.5, 0.5); each step is a typed field with a named trap ('18 is out of 24, not out of 100').

widgets.where: Challenge Section 3 items s3_e1, s3_e3, s3_6, s3_7
widgets.component: 25 points on a 4-block bar, Deshawn's 35 of 50 via 10%, what percent of 250 is 40, what percent of 20 is 35
widgets.root: Percent from part and whole, including above 100%, by the scaling method; in scope.

widgets.where: Challenge Section 3 items s3_e2, s3_1, s3_2, s3_8, s3_9
widgets.component: 10% and 30% of 70, 35% of 80 by benchmarks, 120% of 45, 25% off $64 (discount and sale price), 85% of 40 points
widgets.root: Finding a percent OF a number (benchmarks, discount, Part = Percent × Whole) is lessons 4-3 and 4-4, taught after this one; 4-1 students have no method for it.
widgets.replacement: Delete. Replace with 4-1 items on the same contexts that ask for the percent, not the part: 'A $64 jacket is $16 off: what percent of the price is the discount?' (16 out of 64 scaled to 100), 'Maya earned 34 of 40 points: what percent?', 'A plant is 54 cm tall, 45 cm last month: what percent of last month's height?' (120%), each with a percent bar to build.

widgets.where: Challenge Section 3 items s3_3, s3_4, s3_5, s3_10
widgets.component: 24 is 30% of a number, 52 MB is 65% of the file, 42 is 150% of a number, $2.40 is 6% of a trip
widgets.root: Finding the whole from a part and a percent is lesson 4-5 (its worked example is this method, by 10% steps). Four lessons early.
widgets.replacement: Delete. Replace with 'which grid / bar shows the whole?' items that keep it as a model task: show 30 squares shaded on a grid that is 'the whole' of 100 and ask for the percent, then show a bar where the whole is unknown and ask only for the percent of the whole that is shaded (no solving for the whole).

widgets.where: Challenge Section 4 items s4_e1, s4_1, s4_6, s4_7
widgets.component: 3 of 4 bottles, Team A 75% versus Team B 70%, band is 125% of chorus and chorus is 80% of band, Ben adds 60 to both terms
widgets.root: Percent as a rate per 100, comparison of equal-scale percents, which group is the whole, and the additive misconception are all 4-1 ideas; keys verified.

widgets.where: Challenge Section 4 items s4_e2, s4_2, s4_3, s4_4, s4_5, s4_8
widgets.component: 10% off $40, 25% / 37.5% of 32 students, 30% off then a $5 coupon, 8% tax and 20% tip on $45, 6 L is 40% of a mix, successive 20% + 20% discounts
widgets.root: Percent of a number, sale price, tax and tip are 4-3 / 4-4; the whole from the part is 4-5; successive percent changes (s4_8, and quiz q8 '10% off then 10% off the new price') are in no lesson of Unit 4.
widgets.replacement: Delete. Replace with six 4-1 stories: the percent of a class that walks (8 of 32), a comparison of two surveys with different wholes by scaling both to 100, 140% of a goal, 'which is more, 3/5 of a bar or 55 on a 100-grid', one additive-scaling error detective and one 'percent of the wrong whole' error detective (e.g. 12 of 40 is 12%?).

widgets.component: 14 of 35 = 40%, 9/8 as a percent, 'which statement is always true' (doubling is 200%)
widgets.root: On objective. The other seven quiz items (q1, q2, q5, q6, q7, q8, q10) are covered in the MISALIGNED rows above.

widgets.component: 'Match the Trios' with percents above 100% and below 1%
widgets.root: Same recall-and-decimal-shift matching as the core page; the hard cases (0.25%) are only harder to type, not to understand, and the page has no model to look at.
widgets.replacement: Use the same grid-naming rebuild as the core Bonus Round, with 2-3 grids for 125-300% and a zoomed cell for 0.1-0.8%: the student chooses which picture shows the percent.

formulaOrder.formula: Part = Percent × Whole (percent of a number, benchmarks, discount)
Whole = Part ÷ Percent (whole from part and percent)
fraction / decimal / percent conversion rules (×100, ÷100, divide numerator by denominator)
